decision.observation: The car is at 3 mph in gear 1, sitting on the tarmac with its headlight beam spilling onto the left shoulder; the road ahead curves gently left and then right past a blue puddle, with white posts on both sides. All dots are dark.
decision.hypothesis: Speed keeps bleeding away because each steering input scrubs momentum and the car keeps scraping edges. Plain throttle without steering should rebuild speed while the car is roughly aligned with the lane.
decision.memory: Repeated small steering corrections are costing more speed than they gain. On gentle curves here, straight throttle is the better default.
